title: Customer Concentration Schedule

origin.publisher: District of Columbia Water and Sewer Authority (DC Water)
origin.title: FY2025 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report, Statistical Section (Exhibits 6 and 7, pages 11-12)
origin.clearance_note: Pages 11 and 12 of the 34-page statistical section of DC Water's FY2025 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report, which the authority publishes on its own website for bondholders and the public; downloaded by script. Only Exhibit 6 (Ten Largest Commercial Customers) and Exhibit 7 (Ten Largest Government Customers) are used. No personal data: every customer is a university, hospital, company or government agency. The source PDF's document metadata was cleared when the pages were split out.

notes: Features the FY2025 column of Exhibit 6 on page 1, so the overlay reads as one concentration answer: in fiscal 2025 the largest commercial customer, Georgetown University, paid $7,184 thousand, and the ten largest together paid $37,071 thousand, 3.69% of total operating revenues. A public utility's ACFR stands in for a diligence schedule because no private company's per-customer concentration schedule is published. The request's notes suggested four fields: the FY2025 top commercial customer and amount, the FY2025 top-ten total, the FY2025 percentage, and the schedule title. All but the title shipped, with the fiscal year header added. The title was dropped because inspect_fields marks schedule_title OFF: the extracted value joins the title lines, while its range covers the whole 'EXHIBIT 6 / TEN LARGEST COMMERCIAL CUSTOMERS' block with an HTML line break between them. Each field is pinned to occurrence 0: extraction also returns a second, zero-length range for most fields, which resolves to no page. The '-' cells in the ten-year grid come back as null rather than 0, after the schema made those amounts nullable; the first extraction with plain number types returned 0 for every '-'.
